solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bird in farm out by trade centre

parts.note: a mart is a market, a centre of trade
to let property is to farm it out to a tenant

explanation.surface: A bird spotted on a farm that is rented out near a market town.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the two parts in reverse order; 'by' simply puts them side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A martlet is a heraldic swallow-like bird, and an old dialect name for the house martin.

clue.text: Bug possibly running riot in Minorca — so grim

indicators.note: letters running riot are thrown into wild disorder, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker in Minorca catches a nasty bug that spreads wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running riot' rearranges MINORCA, SO and GRIM; 'possibly' flags that a bug is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ or bug is a familiar example of a tiny living organism seen under a microscope.

clue.text: Bred on a farm, can herd run free?

indicators.note: letters allowed to run free scatter into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A question about whether farmed livestock can be herded loose across open land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run free' rearranges CAN and HERD.
explanation.definitionFit: To ranch animals is to rear them on a large stock farm, so ranched animals were raised there.

clue.text: Insect left floating on river

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece floating on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England (there are several)

explanation.surface: A bug left drifting on the surface of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a common English river name in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A louse is a small wingless parasitic bug living on hair or feathers.

clue.text: Unspecified objects may be such — no good, that is, for keeping

indicators.note: one word keeping others holds them inside it

parts.note: such a thing is this thing
IE (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: A vague remark that nameless objects might be useless, kept for no reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such' looks part of the definition's sentence but is the outer piece; 'for keeping' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Thingies is the casual word for items whose names you cannot recall or do not specify.

clue.text: Old instrument about to be presented to guitarist

indicators.note: the first piece is presented to, placed before, the second

parts.note: RE means about or concerning
Jeff Beck was a celebrated British rock guitarist

explanation.surface: An antique instrument about to be handed to a guitarist.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeff Beck was an English guitarist with the Yardbirds and later solo.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebeck is a medieval bowed string instrument, a forerunner of the fiddle.

clue.text: Irish revolutionary to celebrate Dublin's Easter event?

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to sing is to celebrate, as in singing someone's praises

explanation.surface: An Irish rebel invited to celebrate a famous Dublin anniversary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' signals the turnaround. The Easter Rising of 1916 was the armed rebellion in Dublin against British rule.
explanation.definitionFit: The Easter Rising is the Dublin insurrection of 1916; a rising is an uprising or rebellion.

clue.text: Writer Pearl's old letter found in shrub

parts.note: Pearl S. Buck was the American author of The Good Earth
thorn is an Old English runic letter for the th sound

explanation.surface: An old letter by the novelist Pearl Buck turns up in a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckthorn is a thorny bush of the genus Rhamnus, often found in hedgerows.

clue.text: A record I found in bed — it's mine

indicators.note: these pieces are found inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: Someone discovers an old record in a bed and claims it as theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like a possessive (it's mine) but is a noun, a pit dug for coal.
explanation.definitionFit: A coalpit is a pit from which coal is dug, a type of colliery or mine.

clue.text: Philosopher to study flowering plants, might you say?

indicators.note: signals that the words are matched by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: to con is to study, and fuchsias are flowering plants: con fuchsias

explanation.surface: A philosopher who wants to study flowering plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Confucius was the ancient Chinese sage whose teachings founded Confucianism.

clue.text: Bankruptcy when Conservative gets impetuous

parts.note: rash means hasty or impetuous

explanation.surface: Financial ruin follows when a Tory acts impulsively.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash is a sudden financial collapse, as of a business or market, leading to ruin.

clue.text: Style of country's representative — can be explosive if cut short

definitions.text: can be explosive if cut short

explanation.surface: An ambassador's formal title is said to be explosive when shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: The title is abbreviated HE, which is also the usual abbreviation for high explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the formal style of address for an ambassador; shortened to initials it gives HE, high explosive.

clue.text: Colour of mineral cladding little church

indicators.note: the mineral clads, covers round, the church abbreviation

parts.note: ore is mineral-bearing rock
CH is an abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: The hue of a mineral facing applied to a small chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a yellowish-brown earth pigment and the shade named after it.

clue.text: Biological groups from Egypt, ones in misplaced order

indicators.note: letters put in the wrong order are rearranged

explanation.surface: Biologists sorting Egyptian specimens into groups, but in a muddled order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in misplaced order' rearranges EGYPT and ONES.
explanation.definitionFit: Genotypes are groups of organisms sharing the same genetic constitution.

clue.text: Artist gets rid of bits of salad

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a standard abbreviation for an artist
to dish is informally to ruin or get rid of, as in dishing a rival's hopes

explanation.surface: A painter clears away pieces of salad from the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Radishes are crisp red root vegetables often sliced into a salad.

clue.text: Sign as junior clerk?

parts.note: sub means subordinate or junior
a scribe is a clerk or copyist

explanation.surface: A question whether someone is signing as a lowly office clerk.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a cryptic hint too: a sub-scribe is a junior clerk.
explanation.definitionFit: To subscribe is literally to write one's name underneath, that is to sign a document.

clue.text: Woo heartless old lover? What's the matter with your brain?

definitions.text: What's the matter with your brain?

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter is removed

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Wooing a cruel former partner, someone asks what is wrong with your head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle U of COURT. The definition plays on grey matter: the cortex is the matter of the brain.
explanation.definitionFit: The cerebral cortex is the outer layer of grey matter forming the surface of the brain.

clue.text: Nimble manoeuvring to capture the man in battle

indicators.note: the rearranged letters capture another piece, holding it inside
manoeuvring moves the letters around into a new order

parts.note: he refers to the man

explanation.surface: Agile military manoeuvres to seize an enemy officer during a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvring' gives BLENIM, which 'to capture' then wraps round the man.
explanation.definitionFit: Blenheim, 1704, was the Duke of Marlborough's great victory in the War of the Spanish Succession.

clue.text: 1 down in aged garment

definitions.note: refers back to the bug, a tiny organism

parts.note: AE (Latin aetatis) is the abbreviation for aged, as on gravestones
a robe is a long garment

explanation.surface: A germ lurking in an old item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 down' points to the answer of that clue, a tiny living thing; AE is the Latin abbreviation for aged.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerobe is a tiny organism that needs oxygen to live, so one kind of microbe.

clue.text: Expressed discontent as leftie with inner ache

indicators.note: the second piece goes inside the first, as its inner part

parts.note: a red is a left-winger, a communist
to pine is to ache or yearn

explanation.surface: A left-winger grumbling about a pain deep inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leftie' suggests a left-handed person, but here it is a political red; 'with inner' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To repine is to fret or complain, so having repined someone voiced their unhappiness.

clue.text: Out-of-date language making one's lord seem silly

indicators.note: making the letters seem silly scrambles them into nonsense order

explanation.surface: Speaking an archaic tongue makes a nobleman look foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seem silly' rearranges ONES and LORD; the S of 'one's' is needed here.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Norse is the medieval Scandinavian tongue of the Vikings, no longer spoken.

clue.text: Children, but not one of them joining bank, becoming investor

indicators.note: means the word for one of them is taken away

parts.note: one of the children is a child
a tier is a row or bank, as of seats

explanation.surface: Children, minus one, are linked to a bank and turn into investors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes CHILD from CHILDREN, leaving REN; 'joining' sets TIER beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rentier lives on income from investments or property, so is a type of investor.

clue.text: Disciple having minimal energy within who wanted to depart peacefully?

indicators.note: the energy letter sits within the disciple's name

parts.note: Simon (Peter, or Simon the Zealot) was one of the twelve disciples
E is the abbreviation for energy, at its minimum one letter

explanation.surface: A follower with very little energy who wished to slip away quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: In Luke's gospel Simeon, having seen the infant Jesus, says 'Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace' (the Nunc Dimittis).
explanation.definitionFit: Simeon prayed to be allowed to leave this life in peace, the biblical Nunc Dimittis.

clue.text: Deed by little devil means things getting pushed together

indicators.note: the deed is put beside the devil, after it

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
an action is a deed

explanation.surface: A deed done by a mischievous imp is a way of shoving things together.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaction is the state of being firmly packed or wedged together, as with an impacted tooth.

clue.text: Writer and American gangster seen to be punishable

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
Al Capone was the notorious American gangster

explanation.surface: An author and an American mobster seen to deserve punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Penal relates to punishment, so a penal offence is one liable to be punished.

clue.text: Fruit company producing annual publication

explanation.surface: A fruit firm that also publishes a yearly book.
explanation.walkthrough: Pears, the British soap maker, published the annual Pears' Cyclopaedia for many years.
explanation.definitionFit: These are sweet juicy fruits; the soap firm of that name issued a well-known yearly reference book.

clue.text: Workers by major road where there's a bridge

indicators.note: the road is placed beside the workers

parts.note: men are workers, as in management and men
the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: Labourers by a trunk road near a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the great road from London to Edinburgh; the 1 doubles as the letter I. The Menai Strait in Wales has Telford's famous suspension bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Menai Strait between Anglesey and mainland Wales is crossed by Telford's suspension bridge.

clue.text: Not a plan for promotion

explanation.surface: Getting promoted was never part of a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: In architectural drawing a plan shows a building from above, while the other view shows a face from the side.
explanation.definitionFit: An architect's side view of a building contrasts with a plan; raising someone in rank is also called this.

clue.text: Gradually get into position of advantage at home

parts.note: to have the edge is to hold an advantage
in means at home

explanation.surface: Slowly working one's way into a favourable spot on home ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge in is to insinuate oneself or move in little by little.

clue.text: Unhappy person hoards pounds, being this?

definitions.text: Unhappy person hoards pounds, being this?

indicators.note: one piece hoards another, keeping it inside

parts.note: a misery is a gloomy, unhappy person
L (libra) is the abbreviation for pounds

explanation.surface: A glum person stockpiling cash, which describes such a person exactly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hoards' puts L inside MISERY; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sits on money and spends grudgingly is stingy, the very picture of a skinflint.
